decisions.choice: the commanders of the forces and Johanan: the officers who had gathered at Mizpah and rescued the captives from Ishmael
decisions.reason: These are the army officers who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah (40:7-8). After Ishmael murdered Gedaliah, Johanan and the commanders freed the people Ishmael had taken and brought them to Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem, on the way to Egypt, because they feared what Babylon would do (41:11-18). This chapter goes on from there.

decisions.choice: Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, as the Hebrew reads here
alternatives: Azariah son of Hoshaiah, as the Hebrew reads at 43:2
Azariah, as the Greek translation reads here
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names this leader Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah. In 43:2, where the same leaders reply to Jeremiah, the Hebrew has Azariah son of Hoshaiah, and the Greek translation (the Septuagint, where this chapter is chapter 49) is said to have Azariah here as well. The two names may belong to one man, or one form may have come in from the other in copying. A Jezaniah son of the Maacathite is named among the commanders in 40:8 (Jaazaniah in 2 Kings 25:23), but his father is not Hoshaiah, so he may be someone else. The Hebrew is followed. The description of the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: from the small to the great: everyone, whatever their rank
decisions.reason: The pair takes in the whole people, from the least important to the most important (6:13; 8:10; 2 Kings 25:26). The request comes from everyone, not from the leaders alone.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse (Literal)
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on into verse 2, where the people speak. Balanced and Readable end the sentence here.

decisions.choice: came to Jeremiah; army commanders; least important to the most important
decisions.reason: Readable names Jeremiah, whom they approach (verse 2), and explains "small" and "great" as rank.

decisions.choice: let our plea fall before you: please accept our request
decisions.reason: A request is pictured as falling or being laid down before the person asked, as one bows before a superior. The same phrase is used for a plea to the king in 37:20 and 38:26, and for prayer to God in 36:7. The people show Jeremiah great respect.

decisions.choice: the LORD your God: the people speak of the LORD as Jeremiah's God
decisions.reason: They say "your God", as if the LORD were the prophet's God more than theirs. Jeremiah answers that he will pray to "your God", the God of all of them (verse 4), and in verse 6 the people say "the LORD our God". The shift of pronouns runs through the chapter and returns in verse 20.

decisions.choice: remnant: the few people left in Judah after the fall of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The word means what is left over. Here it is the small group that remained in the land after the exile of 586 BC and the murder of Gedaliah (40:11, 15). The prophets speak of a remnant both as the sign of a disaster and as the seed of hope (Isaiah 10:20-22).

decisions.choice: hear our request (B); listen to what we ask (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1); Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: There were many of us, but only a few are left
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "we are left a few from many" is unfolded into two clauses. Balanced and Readable end the sentence here, and verse 3 follows as a new sentence; Literal keeps one sentence with a comma.

decisions.choice: tu Dios (Jeremiah addressed as tú)
decisions.reason: The people speak to Jeremiah alone, so "your God" is singular here and in verses 3 and 5; the plural_you spans begin when Jeremiah answers all of them (verse 4).

decisions.choice: "ce reste" (L, B); "nous tous qui restons" (R)

decisions.choice: the LORD your God: Jeremiah says "your" to all of them, claiming the LORD as the people's God too
decisions.reason: The people said "your God" to Jeremiah alone (verse 2). Jeremiah answers with the plural "your": the LORD is the God of all of them, not only of the prophet. In verse 6 they take this up and say "our God".

decisions.choice: look, I am praying: I will pray now, as a promise
decisions.reason: The word "look" with a participle announces what the speaker is about to do. Jeremiah agrees at once.

decisions.choice: I will not hold back a word: I will tell everything, whether you like it or not
decisions.reason: The verb means to withhold or keep back. Jeremiah promises to tell them the whole answer, as God told him at his call (1:7, 17) and in 26:2. Verses 19-22 show that the answer was not the one they wanted.

decisions.choice: as you ask (B); as you have asked (R)

decisions.choice: may the LORD be a witness against us: a solemn oath calling on God to judge them if they break their word
decisions.reason: An oath called God to witness, so that he would punish the one who did not keep it (Genesis 31:50; 1 Samuel 12:5; Micah 1:2). The people bind themselves in the strongest way they can, and verses 20-21 hold them to it.

decisions.choice: true and faithful: a witness who will tell exactly what happened and can be relied on
decisions.reason: The two words come from the same root, which speaks of what is firm and reliable. Together they describe a witness who cannot be mistaken or bribed.

decisions.choice: if not ... so we will do: a promise in the form of an oath, "if we do not do it"
decisions.reason: Hebrew oaths often state the condition and leave the curse unspoken, or put it first as here: may God witness against us if we do not act. The sense is a firm promise to obey.

decisions.choice: the condition first: If we fail to do (B) / If we do not do (R) ..., may the LORD be ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the "if" clause before the oath, so the long sentence reads more easily; the sense is unchanged (m3).

decisions.choice: listen to the voice of the LORD: obey him
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is to do what he says (7:23; 26:13). The phrase frames the verse, and verse 21 says they did not do it.

decisions.choice: we: the full form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have a short form of the word "we", found only rarely; the scribes marked the usual longer form to be read aloud (qere). Both mean the same.

decisions.choice: so that it may go well with us: the promise of the covenant
decisions.reason: The words echo the promises of Deuteronomy for those who obey (Deuteronomy 5:33; 6:3) and of Jeremiah 7:23. The people use them of themselves now; they turn on them in verses 20-22.

decisions.choice: obey

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's speech runs from here to the end of the chapter
decisions.reason: Jeremiah speaks from verse 9 to verse 22. In verses 9-18 he gives God's answer, in which God speaks of himself as "I"; in verses 19-22 he speaks in his own voice and warns them (43:1 says he then finished speaking).

decisions.choice: to lay your plea before him: the same picture as in verse 2
decisions.reason: The people asked that their plea "fall" before Jeremiah (verse 2); here the causative form of the same verb says that Jeremiah made it fall, that is, laid it, before God. He reminds them that the answer is to their own request.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (L); he says this (B); This is what the LORD ... says (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Isaiah and Jeremiah. Balanced puts the clause "to whom you sent me" first, so that the long title does not stand between the LORD and "says this". As in 28:16, God's words given by the prophet inside his own speech take no further quotation marks.

decisions.choice: You sent me to him with your request, and this is his answer
decisions.reason: Readable puts the relative clause in a sentence of its own and supplies "this is his answer" to lead into verse 10.

decisions.choice: Así dice el SEÑOR (L); él dice esto (B); Esto es lo que dice el SEÑOR (R)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula set for the prophets, fitted to the sentence as the English does.

decisions.choice: if you will indeed stay: the doubled verb stresses the condition
alternatives: if you will return and stay
decisions.reason: Hebrew strengthens a verb by putting a form of the same verb before it. Here the first word is spelled as if from the verb "return", while the second is "stay". It is best taken as a spelling of the same verb "stay", with one letter dropped, since the whole verse is about remaining in the land (verse 13). Reading it as "return" would give "if you will go back and stay", that is, give up the road to Egypt (41:17).

decisions.choice: build, tear down, plant, uproot: the verbs of Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: These are words from 1:10, where Jeremiah is set over the nations "to uproot and to tear down ... to build and to plant". As in 24:6, only building and planting are promised, and tearing down and uprooting are ruled out, but here the promise depends on the people staying in the land.

decisions.choice: I relent concerning the disaster: God grieves over the judgment he has carried out and turns from it
alternatives: I am sorry for the disaster
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 18:8 and 26:3, where God says he will relent from a disaster he has announced. Here the disaster has already happened: the fall of Jerusalem. The verb also carries the sense of being moved to pity or grieved (Judges 2:18; 2 Samuel 24:16). God is not saying that the judgment was wrong (Numbers 23:19), but that he takes no pleasure in it and has now turned from it, so that he can build and plant again.

decisions.choice: build ... and not tear down ... plant ... and not uproot
decisions.reason: The verbs of 1:10 keep their wording at each level, worded as in 24:6. Balanced and Readable join the two halves with "and", as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: grieves me, and I have relented
decisions.reason: In 18:8 and 26:3 Readable says "change my mind" about a disaster not yet sent. Here it has already come, so Readable names both senses of the verb (m3): grief over the disaster and turning from it. "Relented" is kept from Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: edificar ... derribar ... plantar ... arrancar
decisions.reason: The words of 1:10, kept the same each time they return in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: me pesa (L, B); Me duele ... y he cambiado de parecer (R)
decisions.reason: God relenting (nicham) is never "arrepentirse" in this translation. Here the disaster has already come and the verb carries grief over it (meaning decision m3), so Literal and Balanced say "me pesa", as 1 Samuel 15:11 Literal; elsewhere in Jeremiah Literal says "retractarse".

decisions.choice: "kujenga ... kubomoa ... kupanda ... kung'oa" at every level
decisions.reason: The four verbs of Jeremiah's call (1:10) are kept the same each time they return, so the echo can be heard.

decisions.choice: nimeghairi (L, B); nimebadili nia yangu (R)
decisions.reason: God relenting (*niḥam*) has one wording in Jeremiah: "kughairi" at Literal and Balanced, "kubadili nia" at Readable, as 4:28, 18:8, 10 and 26:3, 13, 19.

decisions.choice: "je renonce au malheur" (L, B), as 18:8 and 26:3
decisions.reason: God relenting (*niḥam*) is "renoncer à" at Literal and Balanced throughout Jeremiah, as Exodus 32:14 in French ("se repentir" would suggest turning from sin); Readable names the grief and the turning, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "bâtir ... démolir ... planter ... arracher"
decisions.reason: The verbs of Jeremiah’s call (1:10), kept the same each time they return.

es.B: No {{plural_you:teman|temáis}} al rey de Babilonia, aunque ahora le {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo. No lo {{plural_you:teman|temáis}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Yo estoy con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:los|os}} salvaré y {{plural_you:los|os}} libraré de su poder.
es.R: No {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo del rey de Babilonia. Sé que le {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} miedo, pero no {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} miedo de él, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Yo estoy con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Los|Os}} salvaré y {{plural_you:los|os}} libraré de su poder.

fr.L: N’ayez pas peur du roi de Babylone, dont vous avez peur ; n’ayez pas peur de lui, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, car je suis avec vous pour vous sauver et pour vous délivrer de sa main.
fr.B: Ne craignez pas le roi de Babylone, même si vous en avez peur maintenant. Ne le craignez pas, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Je suis avec vous, je vous sauverai et je vous délivrerai de son pouvoir.
fr.R: N’ayez pas peur du roi de Babylone. Je sais que vous le craignez, mais n’ayez pas peur de lui, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Je suis avec vous. Je vous sauverai et je vous délivrerai de son pouvoir.

sw.L: Msimwogope mfalme wa Babeli, mnayemwogopa; msimwogope, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana mimi niko pamoja nanyi ili kuwaokoa na kuwaponya na mkono wake.
sw.B: Msimwogope mfalme wa Babeli, ingawa sasa mnamwogopa. Msimwogope, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Mimi niko pamoja nanyi, nami nitawaokoa na kuwaponya na mamlaka yake.
sw.R: Msimwogope mfalme wa Babeli. Najua mnamwogopa, lakini msimwogope, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Mimi niko pamoja nanyi. Nitawaokoa na kuwaponya na mamlaka yake.

decisions.choice: the fear of the king of Babylon: they expected him to punish them for the murder of his governor
decisions.reason: Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, whom Nebuchadnezzar had set over the land, and the Babylonian soldiers with him (41:2-3). Johanan and the others feared that the king would take revenge on all who were left (41:18).

decisions.choice: I am with you to save you and to deliver you: the promise once given to Jeremiah, now given to the people
decisions.reason: God made the same promise to Jeremiah at his call and when he complained (1:8, 19; 15:20). Now it is offered to the whole remnant, as in 30:10-11, if they stay.

decisions.choice: from his hand: from his power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control.

decisions.choice: his power
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m3). Readable also says "I know you fear him" to keep the repeated fear of the Hebrew in plain words.

source.text: וְאֶתֵּ֥ן לָכֶ֛ם רַחֲמִ֖ים וְרִחַ֣ם אֶתְכֶ֑ם וְהֵשִׁ֥יב אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֶל־אַדְמַתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will give to you compassion, and he will have compassion on you and he will return you to your soil.

en.L: And I will grant you compassion, and he will have compassion on you and bring you back to your own soil.
en.B: I will grant you compassion, so that he will have compassion on you and let you return to your own land.
en.R: I will make the king show you mercy. He will be kind to you and let you go back to your own land.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:les|os}} daré compasión, y él tendrá compasión de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:los|os}} hará volver a {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} concederé compasión, para que él tenga compasión de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:los|os}} deje volver a {{plural_you:su propia tierra|vuestra propia tierra}}.
es.R: Haré que el rey tenga compasión de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Será bueno con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y {{plural_you:los|os}} dejará volver a {{plural_you:su tierra|vuestra tierra}}.

fr.L: Et je vous accorderai la compassion, et il aura compassion de vous et vous fera revenir sur votre sol.
fr.B: Je vous accorderai la compassion, et il aura compassion de vous et vous laissera revenir sur votre terre.
fr.R: Je ferai en sorte que le roi ait pitié de vous. Il sera bon pour vous et vous laissera retourner sur votre terre.

sw.L: Nami nitawapa rehema, naye atawarehemu na kuwarudisha katika ardhi yenu.
sw.B: Nitawapa rehema, ili naye awarehemu na kuwaruhusu mrudi katika nchi yenu.
sw.R: Nitamfanya mfalme awaonyeshe huruma. Atawatendea wema na kuwaruhusu mrudi katika nchi yenu.

decisions.choice: I will grant you compassion: I will cause you to find compassion from the king
decisions.reason: To "give someone compassion" is to make others treat him with pity (1 Kings 8:50; Nehemiah 1:11; Psalm 106:46). God will move the king of Babylon to be kind to them.

decisions.choice: he will bring you back, as the Hebrew reads
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "he will cause you to return". Since the people are still in the land, a change of one vowel would give "he will let you stay" (from the verb "stay" in verse 10), and the Greek translation is said to read "I will bring you back". The Hebrew makes sense as it stands: the people had fled from Mizpah and were camped on the road to Egypt (41:16-17), and many had scattered to nearby lands (40:11-12). The king will let them go back to their homes. The description of the Greek is from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: your own soil: the farmland of their own homes
decisions.reason: The word is the ground that is farmed, not only the country. It fits the promise to plant them (verse 10).

decisions.choice: the king; be kind to you
decisions.reason: Readable names the king, whom "he" refers to (verse 11), and spreads "compassion" over "mercy" and "kind".

source.text: וְאִם־אֹמְרִ֣ים אַתֶּ֔ם לֹ֥א נֵשֵׁ֖ב בָּאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את לְבִלְתִּ֣י שְׁמֹ֔עַ בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And if [are] saying you: not we will stay in the land the this, so as not to listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God,

en.L: But if you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' so as not to listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God,
en.B: But suppose you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' and so disobey the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God,
en.R: But you may say, 'We will not stay in this land.' You may refuse to obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

es.L: Pero si {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “No nos quedaremos en esta tierra”, para no escuchar la voz {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}},
es.B: Pero supongamos que {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “No nos quedaremos en esta tierra”, y así {{plural_you:desobedecen|desobedecéis}} la voz {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}},
es.R: Pero tal vez {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: “No nos quedaremos en esta tierra”. Tal vez se {{plural_you:nieguen|neguéis}} a obedecer {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}.

fr.L: Mais si vous dites : “Nous ne demeurerons pas dans ce pays”, pour ne pas écouter la voix {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu,
fr.B: Mais supposons que vous disiez : “Nous ne resterons pas dans ce pays”, et que vous désobéissiez ainsi à la voix {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} votre Dieu,
fr.R: Mais vous direz peut-être : “Nous ne resterons pas dans ce pays.” Vous refuserez peut-être d’obéir {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} votre Dieu.

sw.L: Lakini mkisema, 'Hatutakaa katika nchi hii,' hata msiisikilize sauti ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu,
sw.B: Lakini tuseme mnasema, 'Hatutakaa katika nchi hii,' na hivyo mnaiasi sauti ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu,
sw.R: Lakini huenda mkasema, 'Hatutakaa katika nchi hii.' Huenda mkakataa kumtii {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu.

decisions.choice: but if you say: the second choice, set against verses 10-12
decisions.reason: Verse 10 began "if you stay"; here begins the other path. The condition runs through verses 13-15, and the result is given in verses 16-17.

decisions.choice: so as not to listen to the voice of the LORD: refusing to obey him
decisions.reason: Saying "we will not stay" would itself be the refusal to obey. The words recall the people's oath in verse 6.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The sentence goes on through verses 14-16. Readable uses short sentences and picks up the condition again in verse 15.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks
decisions.reason: The words the people might say are quoted inside Jeremiah's speech, which is already in double quotation marks.

source.text: לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹ֚א כִּ֣י אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ נָב֔וֹא אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־נִרְאֶה֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה וְק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָ֖ר לֹ֣א נִשְׁמָ֑ע וְלַלֶּ֥חֶם לֹֽא־נִרְעָ֖ב וְשָׁ֥ם נֵשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: saying: no, for [the] land of Egypt we will go, where not we will see war, and [the] sound of [the] shofar not we will hear, and for bread not we will hunger, and there we will stay,

en.L: saying, 'No, but to the land of Egypt we will go, where we will not see war or hear the sound of the trumpet or be hungry for bread, and there we will stay,'
en.B: and say, 'No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will see no war, hear no ram's horn sounding and never go hungry for bread. That is where we will live,'
en.R: You may say, 'No! We will go to Egypt. There we will not see war or hear the trumpet call to battle. We will never be hungry there. That is where we will live.'

es.B: y {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “No, iremos a la tierra de Egipto, donde no veremos guerra, no oiremos el sonido del cuerno de carnero y nunca pasaremos hambre. Allí es donde viviremos”,
es.R: Tal vez {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: “¡No! Iremos a Egipto. Allí no veremos guerra ni oiremos la trompeta que llama a la batalla. Allí nunca pasaremos hambre. Allí es donde viviremos”.

fr.L: disant : “Non, mais c’est au pays d’Égypte que nous irons, où nous ne verrons pas la guerre et n’entendrons pas le son du cor et n’aurons pas faim de pain, et là nous demeurerons”,
fr.B: et que vous disiez : “Non, nous irons au pays d’Égypte, où nous ne verrons pas de guerre, n’entendrons pas sonner le cor et ne manquerons jamais de pain. C’est là que nous habiterons”,
fr.R: Vous direz peut-être : “Non ! Nous irons en Égypte. Là, nous ne verrons pas la guerre et nous n’entendrons pas la trompette qui appelle au combat. Nous n’aurons jamais faim là-bas. C’est là que nous habiterons.”

sw.L: mkisema, 'Hapana, bali tutakwenda nchi ya Misri, ambako hatutaona vita, wala hatutasikia sauti ya baragumu, wala hatutaona njaa ya mkate, nasi tutakaa huko,'
sw.B: na kusema, 'Hapana, tutakwenda nchi ya Misri, ambako hatutaona vita, hatutasikia sauti ya baragumu, wala hatutaona njaa ya chakula. Huko ndiko tutakakoishi,'
sw.R: Huenda mkasema, 'Hapana! Tutakwenda Misri. Huko hatutaona vita wala kusikia baragumu ikiita vitani. Hatutaona njaa kamwe huko. Huko ndiko tutakakoishi.'

decisions.choice: the sound of the shofar: the alarm that warned of an enemy attack
decisions.reason: The ram's horn was blown to warn of an invading army and to call men to battle (4:5, 19, 21; 6:1). The people want a land where they will never hear it again.

decisions.choice: no, but: a strong refusal followed by the plan they choose instead
decisions.reason: The word "no" answers God's offer to stay, and the next word sets their own plan against it.

decisions.choice: going back to Egypt: turning back the way of the exodus
decisions.reason: Egypt was the land God had brought Israel out of, and the Law warned against going back there (Deuteronomy 17:16; 28:68). The people hope it will be a place of safety and plenty, as it had been in Joseph's time (Genesis 42:1-2). Verses 16-17 answer each of their hopes.

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, R); ram's horn (B)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for the shofar, as in Isaiah. Readable adds "call to battle" to say what the sound meant (m1).

decisions.choice: That is where we will live
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "there" first for stress; Balanced and Readable give the stress with a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: trompeta (L, R); cuerno de carnero (B)
decisions.reason: The *shofar* is a ram's horn blown as an alarm in war; Balanced names it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: baragumu
decisions.reason: The *shofar*, the ram's horn blown as the alarm of war, is "baragumu" at every level, as in 4:5-21 and 6:1, 17; Readable says what it called people to ("ikiita vitani").

en.L: then now, therefore, hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, remnant of Judah. Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: If you indeed set your faces to go to Egypt, and you go to sojourn there,
en.B: then hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, remnant of Judah. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: If you are set on going to Egypt, and you go to settle there,

fr.B: alors écoutez la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, reste de Juda. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci : Si vous êtes décidés à aller en Égypte, et que vous y alliez pour vous y installer,
fr.R: Si vous faites cela, alors écoutez le message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, vous qui restez de Juda. Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël : Si vous avez décidé d’aller vivre en Égypte,

decisions.choice: set your faces to go: be determined to go
decisions.reason: To set one's face toward a place is to make up one's mind to go there (2 Kings 12:18; Jeremiah 44:12). The doubled verb stresses how firm the decision is.

decisions.choice: sojourn: live as outsiders in a land not their own
decisions.reason: The verb is used of living somewhere as a resident foreigner, without the rights of a native (Genesis 12:10; 47:4). Israel's fathers had once gone down to sojourn in Egypt; now the people want to do the same.

decisions.choice: and now, therefore: the result of the condition in verses 13-14
decisions.reason: After the long "if" clause the speech turns to what follows, and then restates the condition in God's words before giving the result in verse 16.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (L); the LORD of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this title in Isaiah and Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: sojourn (L); settle (B); live (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word for living as an outsider (m2); Balanced and Readable use common words.

decisions.choice: If you do that
decisions.reason: Readable broke verses 13-14 into short sentences, so it supplies these words to pick up the condition again.

decisions.choice: se empeñan en ir (L); están decididos a ir (B); han decidido ir (R)
decisions.reason: "Setting the face" toward a place means being determined to go there.

decisions.choice: "sikieni neno la BWANA" (L); "sikilizeni neno la BWANA" (B); "sikilizeni ujumbe huu kutoka kwa BWANA" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for "hear the word of the LORD" in Swahili, as 2 Kings 20:16.

decisions.choice: "écoutez la parole du SEIGNEUR" (L, B); "écoutez le message du SEIGNEUR" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for "hear the word of the LORD" in the French prophets.

source.text: וְהָיְתָ֣ה הַחֶ֗רֶב אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתֶּם֙ יְרֵאִ֣ים מִמֶּ֔נָּה שָׁ֛ם תַּשִּׂ֥יג אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהָרָעָ֞ב אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֣ם׀דֹּאֲגִ֣ים מִמֶּ֗נּוּ שָׁ֣ם יִדְבַּ֧ק אַחֲרֵיכֶ֛ם מִצְרַ֖יִם וְשָׁ֥ם תָּמֻֽתוּ׃

en.L: then the sword that you are afraid of will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine that you dread will cling close behind you there in Egypt, and there you will die.
en.B: then the sword you fear will catch up with you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine you dread will follow close behind you into Egypt, and you will die there.
en.R: then the war you are afraid of will catch up with you there in Egypt. The famine you are worried about will follow you there. And you will die there.

es.L: sucederá que la espada que {{plural_you:temen|teméis}} {{plural_you:los|os}} alcanzará allí, en la tierra de Egipto, y el hambre que {{plural_you:les|os}} preocupa se pegará a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} allí, en Egipto, y allí {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}}.
es.B: entonces la espada que {{plural_you:temen|teméis}} {{plural_you:los|os}} alcanzará allá, en la tierra de Egipto, y el hambre que {{plural_you:les|os}} da miedo {{plural_you:los|os}} seguirá de cerca hasta Egipto, y allí {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}}.

fr.R: alors la guerre dont vous avez peur vous rattrapera là-bas, en Égypte. La famine qui vous inquiète vous suivra jusque là-bas. Et vous y mourrez.

sw.L: ndipo upanga mnaouogopa utawapata huko katika nchi ya Misri, na njaa mnayoihofu itawaandama kwa karibu huko Misri, nanyi mtakufa huko.
sw.B: ndipo upanga mnaouogopa utawafikia huko katika nchi ya Misri, na njaa mnayoihofu itawafuata kwa karibu mpaka Misri, nanyi mtakufa huko.
sw.R: ndipo vita mnavyoviogopa vitawafikia huko Misri. Njaa mnayoihofia itawafuata huko. Nanyi mtakufa huko.

decisions.choice: the sword and famine you fear will find you there: they cannot outrun what they flee
decisions.reason: The people wanted to escape war and hunger (verse 14). The very things they fear will go with them to Egypt. "There" is said three times.

decisions.choice: cling after you: pursue you closely and not let go
decisions.reason: The verb means to stick or cling to something; with "after" it describes a pursuer who keeps close behind (1 Samuel 14:22).

decisions.choice: dread: be anxious, worried
decisions.reason: The word describes anxious worry about what may happen (38:19).

decisions.choice: war
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for the sword, as in the wording set for "sword, famine and pestilence" in Jeremiah.

source.text: וְיִֽהְי֣וּ כָל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֨מוּ אֶת־פְּנֵיהֶ֜ם לָב֤וֹא מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לָג֣וּר שָׁ֔ם יָמ֕וּתוּ בַּחֶ֖רֶב בָּרָעָ֣ב וּבַדָּ֑בֶר וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ שָׂרִ֣יד וּפָלִ֔יט מִפְּנֵי֙ הָֽרָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י מֵבִ֥יא עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And will be all the men who have set their faces to go [to] Egypt to sojourn there, they will die by the sword, by the famine and by the pestilence, and not will be for them a survivor and escapee from before the disaster that I [am] bringing on them.

en.L: And all the {{gender:people|men}} who set their faces to go to Egypt to sojourn there will die by the sword, by the famine and by the pestilence; and none of them will be a survivor or an escapee from the disaster that I am bringing on them.
en.B: All the {{gender:people|men}} who are set on going to Egypt to settle there will die by sword, famine and plague. No one among them will survive or escape the disaster I am bringing on them.
en.R: Everyone who is determined to go and live in Egypt will die from war, famine or disease. Not one of them will live through the disaster I will bring on them or escape from it.

es.L: Y todos {{gender:los que|los hombres que}} se empeñen en ir a Egipto para residir allí morirán por la espada, por el hambre y por la peste; y no habrá de ellos sobreviviente ni quien escape del mal que yo traigo sobre ellos.
es.B: Todos {{gender:los que|los hombres que}} estén decididos a ir a Egipto para establecerse allí morirán por la espada, el hambre y la peste. Ninguno de ellos sobrevivirá ni escapará de la calamidad que traeré sobre ellos.
es.R: Todos los que estén decididos a ir a vivir a Egipto morirán por la guerra, el hambre o las enfermedades. Ninguno de ellos sobrevivirá a la desgracia que traeré sobre ellos, ni escapará de ella.

fr.L: Et tous les {{gender:gens|hommes}} qui ont tourné leurs faces pour aller en Égypte, pour y séjourner en étrangers, mourront par l’épée, par la famine et par la peste ; et il n’y aura pour eux ni survivant ni rescapé devant le malheur que je fais venir sur eux.
fr.B: Tous les {{gender:gens|hommes}} qui sont décidés à aller en Égypte pour s’y installer mourront par l’épée, la famine et la peste. Aucun d’eux ne survivra ni n’échappera au malheur que je fais venir sur eux.
fr.R: Tous ceux qui sont décidés à aller vivre en Égypte mourront de la guerre, de la famine ou de la maladie. Pas un d’entre eux ne survivra au malheur que je ferai venir sur eux, ni ne lui échappera.

sw.L: Na watu wote waliokaza nyuso zao kwenda Misri kukaa huko kama wageni watakufa kwa upanga, kwa njaa na kwa tauni; wala hapatakuwa na yeyote kati yao atakayesalia au kuokoka kutoka katika mabaya nitakayoleta juu yao.
sw.B: Watu wote waliokusudia kwenda Misri kuishi huko watakufa kwa upanga, njaa na tauni. Hakuna hata mmoja wao atakayenusurika wala kuokoka katika maafa nitakayoleta juu yao.
sw.R: Kila mtu aliyeamua kwenda kuishi Misri atakufa kwa vita, njaa au magonjwa. Hakuna hata mmoja wao atakayeyapita salama maafa nitakayoleta juu yao, wala kuyaepuka.

decisions.choice: the men: the people as a whole, women and children with them
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of "man", but here it means all who go to Egypt; women and children went too (43:6; 44:15).

decisions.choice: they will die: God now speaks of them, not to them
decisions.reason: The speech moves from "you" to "they" and back to "you" in verse 18. The change makes the verse sound like a sentence pronounced over everyone who takes that road.

decisions.choice: survivor or escapee: no one at all will come through
decisions.reason: The two words name one who is left alive and one who gets away. Together they mean that none will escape (44:14; Joshua 8:22).

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence (L); sword, famine and plague (B); war, famine or disease (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this list in Jeremiah. Literal keeps "by the" before each word, as the Hebrew does; Readable says "or" because each person dies one way.

decisions.choice: people (default); men (alternative)
decisions.reason: The gender setting, since both sexes are meant (m1). Readable says "everyone", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:los que|los hombres que}}
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "men" here means everyone who goes, women as well as men (44:15 names the women).

decisions.choice: "watu wote" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: "Watu" already includes women and children; the only other wording, "wanaume", would change the meaning.

source.text: כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֮ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ נִתַּ֨ךְ אַפִּ֜י וַחֲמָתִ֗י עַל־יֹֽשְׁבֵי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כֵּ֣ן תִּתַּ֤ךְ חֲמָתִי֙ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם בְּבֹאֲכֶ֖ם מִצְרָ֑יִם וִהְיִיתֶ֞ם לְאָלָ֤ה וּלְשַׁמָּה֙ וְלִקְלָלָ֣ה וּלְחֶרְפָּ֔ה וְלֹֽא־תִרְא֣וּ ע֔וֹד אֶת־הַמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: just as was poured out my anger and my wrath on [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, so will be poured out my wrath on you when you go [to] Egypt, and you will become an oath-curse and a horror and a curse and a reproach, and not you will see again the place the this.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Just as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt; and you will become an execration and a horror, and a curse and a reproach; and you will not see this place again.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: Just as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury were poured out on the people of Jerusalem, so {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become a name used in curses, a horror, a curse and a disgrace, and you will never see this place again.
en.R: For this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I poured out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} great anger on the people of Jerusalem. In the same way I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on you when you go to Egypt. People will use your name when they curse someone. They will be horrified at you, curse you and insult you. You will never see this place again.

es.L: Porque así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, el Dios de Israel: Como se derramó {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor sobre los habitantes de Jerusalén, así se derramará {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cuando {{plural_you:entren|entréis}} en Egipto; y {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} objeto de execración y de horror, de maldición y de oprobio, y no {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} más este lugar.
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: Así como {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor se derramaron sobre la gente de Jerusalén, así se derramará {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cuando {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a Egipto. {{plural_you:Su nombre|Vuestro nombre}} se usará para maldecir; {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} un horror, una maldición y una vergüenza, y nunca más {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} este lugar.
es.R: Porque esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel: Yo derramé {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gran enojo sobre la gente de Jerusalén. De la misma manera derramaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enojo sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cuando {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a Egipto. La gente usará {{plural_you:su nombre|vuestro nombre}} para maldecir a otros. Se horrorizarán al {{plural_you:verlos|veros}}, {{plural_you:los|os}} maldecirán y {{plural_you:los|os}} insultarán. Nunca más {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} este lugar.

fr.L: Car ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël : De même que {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère et {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur se sont déversées sur les habitants de Jérusalem, ainsi {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur se déversera sur vous quand vous irez en Égypte ; et vous deviendrez une exécration et une horreur, une malédiction et un opprobre ; et vous ne verrez plus ce lieu.
fr.B: Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci : De même que {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère et {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur se sont déversées sur les habitants de Jérusalem, ainsi {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur se déversera sur vous quand vous irez en Égypte. Vous deviendrez un nom qu’on utilise pour maudire, un objet d’horreur, une malédiction et un objet de honte, et vous ne reverrez jamais ce lieu.
fr.R: Car voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël : J’ai déversé {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} grande colère sur les habitants de Jérusalem. De la même manière, je déverserai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère sur vous quand vous irez en Égypte. Les gens se serviront de votre nom quand ils voudront maudire quelqu’un. Ils seront horrifiés devant vous, ils vous maudiront et vous insulteront. Vous ne reverrez jamais ce lieu.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi, Mungu wa Israeli: Kama hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} zilivyomwagwa juu ya wakaaji wa Yerusalemu, ndivyo ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itakavyomwagwa juu yenu mtakapokwenda Misri; nanyi mtakuwa kiapo cha laana, na kitisho, na laana, na aibu; wala hamtapaona mahali hapa tena.
sw.B: Kwa maana hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo: Kama hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} zilivyomwagwa juu ya watu wa Yerusalemu, ndivyo ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itakavyomwagwa juu yenu mtakapokwenda Misri. Mtakuwa jina linalotumiwa katika laana, kitisho, laana na aibu, wala hamtapaona mahali hapa tena kamwe.
sw.R: Kwa maana hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema: Nilimwaga hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuu juu ya watu wa Yerusalemu. Vivyo hivyo nitamwaga hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} juu yenu mtakapokwenda Misri. Watu watalitaja jina lenu wanapomlaani mtu. Watawaona kuwa kitisho, watawalaani na kuwatukana. Hamtapaona mahali hapa tena kamwe.

decisions.choice: anger and wrath poured out: God's judgment pictured as something poured out like a liquid
decisions.reason: The picture is used of the fall of Jerusalem (7:20; 44:6). The judgment that fell on the city will fall on those who go to Egypt.

decisions.choice: an execration: a name used in an oath of cursing
decisions.reason: The word is a curse spoken as part of an oath. To "become" one means that people will use your fate as the model for a curse, as in 29:22: "May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and like Ahab."

decisions.choice: execration, horror, curse, reproach: the covenant curses of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: Lists of this kind come from Deuteronomy 28:37 and return in Jeremiah (24:9; 25:18; 29:18; 44:12). They describe a people whose disaster becomes a byword among the nations.

decisions.choice: this place: Judah, their homeland
decisions.reason: The words point to the land where they are standing. Those who go to Egypt will never come back (44:14, 28).

decisions.choice: execration, horror, curse, reproach (L); a name used in curses, a horror, a curse, a disgrace (B); use your name when they curse, horrified, curse, insult (R)
decisions.reason: "Horror" and "curse" follow the wording set for these lists in Jeremiah; "reproach" and "disgrace" follow 24:9. Readable turns the nouns into what people will do.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD of hosts (L); the LORD of Armies ... says this (B); This is what the LORD of Armies ... says (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

decisions.choice: objeto de execración, horror, maldición, oprobio (L); su nombre se usará para maldecir, un horror, una maldición, una vergüenza (B); usará su nombre para maldecir, se horrorizarán, los maldecirán, los insultarán (R)
decisions.reason: The curse list follows the wording set for Jeremiah: *ʾalah* is an execration (L), a name used in curses (B), a curse (R).

decisions.choice: "kiapo cha laana, kitisho, laana, aibu" (L); "jina linalotumiwa katika laana, kitisho, laana, aibu" (B); Readable spells out what people will do
decisions.reason: The wording set for *ʾalah* in these lists: an oath of cursing at Literal, a name used in curses at Balanced, and plain statements at Readable, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "une exécration, une horreur, une malédiction et un opprobre" (L); "un nom qu’on utilise pour maudire, un objet d’horreur, une malédiction et un objet de honte" (B); Readable says what each means
decisions.reason: The curse list as the English sets it for Jeremiah, in the same French throughout the book (24:9; 29:18): *ʾalah* "une exécration" / "un nom qu’on utilise pour maudire", *shammah* "une horreur" / "un objet d’horreur", *ḥerpah* "un opprobre" / "un objet de honte".

source.text: דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה עֲלֵיכֶם֙ שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה אַל־תָּבֹ֖אוּ מִצְרָ֑יִם יָדֹ֨עַ֙ תֵּֽדְע֔וּ כִּי־הַעִידֹ֥תִי בָכֶ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: Has spoken Yahweh to you, remnant of Judah: not go [to] Egypt. Knowing know that I have warned you the day.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken to you, remnant of Judah: 'Do not go to Egypt.' Know for certain that I have warned you this day.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has told you, remnant of Judah, 'Do not go to Egypt.' Know for certain that I have warned you today.
en.R: You people who are left from Judah, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has told you, 'Do not go to Egypt.' You can be sure of this: I have warned you today.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha hablado, remanente de Judá: “No {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a Egipto”. {{plural_you:Sepan|Sabed}} con certeza que hoy {{plural_you:les|os}} he advertido.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dicho, remanente de Judá: “No {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a Egipto”. {{plural_you:Sepan|Sabed}} con certeza que hoy {{plural_you:les|os}} he advertido.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los que quedan de Judá, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dicho: “No {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a Egipto”. {{plural_you:Pueden|Podéis}} estar seguros de esto: hoy {{plural_you:les|os}} he advertido.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a parlé, reste de Juda : “N’allez pas en Égypte.” Sachez bien que je vous ai avertis aujourd’hui.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a dit, reste de Juda : “N’allez pas en Égypte.” Sachez-le bien : je vous ai avertis aujourd’hui.
fr.R: Vous qui restez de Juda, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} vous a dit : “N’allez pas en Égypte.” Vous pouvez en être sûrs : je vous ai avertis aujourd’hui.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema nanyi, enyi mabaki ya Yuda: 'Msiende Misri.' Jueni hakika kwamba nimewaonya leo.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewaambia, enyi mabaki ya Yuda, 'Msiende Misri.' Jueni hakika kwamba nimewaonya leo.
sw.R: Enyi watu mliobaki kutoka Yuda, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewaambia, 'Msiende Misri.' Muwe na hakika na jambo hili: nimewaonya leo.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah now speaks in his own voice
decisions.reason: God's answer ended in verse 18. In verses 19-22 Jeremiah sums it up and warns them, speaking of God as "the LORD" and of himself as "I".

decisions.choice: I have warned you: I have testified against you as a witness
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word "witness". The people called on the LORD as a witness against them (verse 5); now Jeremiah has solemnly warned them, and his warning will stand as evidence against them (Deuteronomy 8:19).

decisions.choice: know for certain: the doubled verb stresses the warning
decisions.reason: As in verse 22. It means "make no mistake".

decisions.choice: You people who are left from Judah
decisions.reason: Readable puts the address first and explains "remnant".

source.text: כִּ֣י הִתְעֵיתֶם֮בְּנַפְשֽׁוֹתֵיכֶם֒ כִּֽי־אַתֶּ֞ם שְׁלַחְתֶּ֣ם אֹתִ֗י אֶל־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בַּעֲדֵ֔נוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וּכְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֹאמַ֜ר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ כֵּ֥ן הַגֶּד־לָ֖נוּ וְעָשִֽׂינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For you have led astray yourselves at the cost of your lives; for you sent me to Yahweh your God, saying: pray for us to Yahweh our God, and according to all that will say Yahweh our God, so tell to us, and we will do.

en.L: For you have led yourselves astray at the cost of your lives; for you yourselves sent me to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, saying, 'Pray for us to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, and according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God says, so tell us, and we will do [it].'
en.B: You have deceived yourselves, and it will cost you your lives. You yourselves sent me to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and said, 'Pray for us to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. Tell us everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God says, and we will do it.'
en.R: You have fooled yourselves, and it will cost you your lives. You sent me to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You said, 'Pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God for us. Tell us everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God says, and we will do it.'

es.L: Porque {{plural_you:se han engañado|os habéis engañado}} a costa de {{plural_you:sus vidas|vuestras vidas}}; pues {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me {{plural_you:enviaron|enviasteis}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, diciendo: “Ora por nosotros {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, y conforme a todo lo que diga {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, así decláranoslo, y [lo] haremos”.
es.B: {{plural_you:Se han engañado|Os habéis engañado}} a {{plural_you:ustedes mismos|vosotros mismos}}, y eso {{plural_you:les|os}} costará la vida. {{plural_you:Ustedes mismos|Vosotros mismos}} me {{plural_you:enviaron|enviasteis}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} y me {{plural_you:dijeron|dijisteis}}: “Ora por nosotros {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} nuestro Dios. Dinos todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios diga, y lo haremos”.

decisions.choice: you have led yourselves astray at the cost of your lives
alternatives: you have gone astray at the cost of your lives
you acted deceitfully in your hearts
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) of the verb differ slightly from the form the scribes marked to be read aloud (qere); both come from a verb meaning "to wander" or, in this form, "to lead astray". The verb usually has an object, and here the phrase after it can mean "against yourselves" or "at the cost of your lives". So the clause may mean that they misled themselves to their own ruin, that they made a fatal mistake, or that they were not honest when they made their oath. Each gives the same warning: their choice will cost them their lives.

decisions.choice: your God ... our God: Jeremiah repeats their own words back to them
decisions.reason: Jeremiah says they sent him to "the LORD your God" and quotes them saying "the LORD our God" (verse 6). They claimed the LORD as their own God but would not do what he said.

decisions.choice: for you yourselves sent me: the pronoun is stressed
decisions.reason: The word "you" is written out for emphasis. The request was theirs; they cannot now treat the answer as Jeremiah's idea (43:2-3).

decisions.choice: deceived yourselves (B); fooled yourselves (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the first sense in m1 and say "it will cost you your lives" for the phrase after the verb.

decisions.choice: you have not listened: Jeremiah speaks of their refusal as already made
decisions.reason: The people do not reply until 43:2-3, but Jeremiah already sees their answer. His words describe what they have decided in their hearts, and the next chapter shows he was right.

decisions.choice: listened to the voice: obeyed
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, where they promised to listen to the voice of the LORD.

decisions.choice: obeyed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m2). Literal supplies "with" to finish the phrase "sent me to you".

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence: the same three as in verse 17
decisions.reason: Jeremiah ends with the sentence God gave in verse 17. The place they long for will be the place of their death.

decisions.choice: desire: want, take pleasure in
decisions.reason: The verb means to delight in or set one's heart on something. It shows that their minds are made up.

decisions.choice: sword, famine and pestilence (L); sword, famine and plague (B); war, famine or disease (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17. Literal keeps the Hebrew order, with the three words before the verb.
